Food industries are businesses that process, preserve, package and distribute food for consumers. Examples include milling, dairy, meat, beverage, bakery and fruit-processing industries. They use raw materials such as maize, milk, fruits, vegetables and meat to produce safe and convenient food products. Food industries create employment, add value to local agricultural products and contribute to economic development.

raw.title: LEARNING ACTIVITY 4: Making up a shopping plan

segs.t: A Form 2 Food and Nutrition class is given K250 to prepare a nutritious meal for a small school activity. The teacher divides the learners into inclusive groups consisting of boys and girls, including a learner with a physical disability. Each group should:
Decide on a balanced meal to prepare.
Check which ingredients are already available in the Food and Nutrition laboratory.
Prepare a shopping list showing the item, quantity, estimated price and total cost.
Ensure that the total cost does not exceed K250.
Suggest ways of reducing food waste and unnecessary packaging.
Ensure that every learner participates according to their abilities.
Present and justify the shopping plan to the class.

replaceBlocks.find: Smart food purchasing requires a mix of financial discipline, safety awareness, and strategic planning. Shoppers must carry backup cash in case digital payment systems fail, and they should always calculate unit pricing since larger packages are occasionally more expensive per gram. Sticking strictly to a shopping list prevents costly impulse buying, while safety checks like avoiding dented or bulging cans must always take priority over written expiry dates. Finally, collaborating with others to buy items in bulk allows everyday consumers to access lower wholesale prices and split costs effectively.
